source: Learner follow-up in conversation after assessment

corrections.classification: learner-reported selection slip; not evidence of failed desert recognition
learner confirms genuine confusion between saa (hour) and sana (year); do not infer a general inflection deficit

process_report: Enjoyed the assessment, although reading stories feels energy-intensive.
Words without tashkeel are sometimes clearly harder; frequently encountered forms can be fine.
For the volunteer item, tried several possible readings mentally; having the meaning among the options helped.
Other words also have confounders; reading a sentence often feels like solving a puzzle.
Occasional sentences that work smoothly feel like magic.
interpretation: Supports an item-dependent difficulty resolving written forms and accessing meanings efficiently. Meaning-choice success can include answer-supported recognition. Does not isolate decoding, lexical access, lexical competition, and sentence integration as independent causes.
next_assessment: Short diagnostic support comparison: separate initial Arabic reading from displayed meaning options, compare fresh matched items with/without vowels with counterbalanced order and answer positions, and examine one short passage before/after targeted support. Collect effort and brief retrospective process reports; do not impose speed thresholds or treat supported rereading gains as transfer.
